import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
try:
    df = pd.read_csv('data/titanic.csv')
except FileNotFoundError:
    df = sns.load_dataset('titanic')

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create a FacetGrid to show survival rates across different categories
# We will look at Class, Sex, and where they Embarked
g = sns.catplot(
    data=df,
    x='class',
    y='survived',
    hue='sex',
    col='embark_town',
    kind='bar',
    palette='viridis',
    height=5,
    aspect=0.8,
    errorbar=None,  # Turn off confidence intervals for a cleaner look
    legend=False  # We will add a custom legend later
)

# Improve the plot with better labels and a main title
g.fig.suptitle('Titanic Survival Rates by Class, Sex, and Port of Embarkation', y=1.03, fontsize=16, fontweight='bold')
g.set_axis_labels("Passenger Class", "Survival Rate")
g.set_titles("Port: {col_name}")
g.despine(left=True)

# Format y-axis ticks as percentages and add data labels
for ax in g.axes.flat:
    # Set y-axis to percentage format
    ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(plt.FuncFormatter(lambda y, _: f'{y:.0%}'))
    ax.set_ylim(0, 1)

    # Add annotations (survival rate percentages) on top of each bar
    for p in ax.patches:
        if p.get_height() > 0:  # Only label bars with a value
            ax.annotate(f"{p.get_height():.1%}",
                        (p.get_x() + p.get_width() / 2., p.get_height()),
                        ha='center', va='center',
                        xytext=(0, 9),
                        textcoords='offset points',
                        fontsize=9.5,
                        color='dimgray',
                        fontweight='semibold')

# Add a single, clear legend to the figure
plt.legend(title='Sex', loc='upper right', bbox_to_anchor=(1.18, 0.95), frameon=True)

# Adjust layout to prevent title overlap
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.97])

# Save the final figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
